messages:
Maya: quick sync — multiple tier-1 customers asked for longer pin/grace paths and pin-exemptions this week. lots of asks across support and sales. can we talk tradeoffs vs our onboarding/bench roadmap for this quarter?

Simon: +1. can you share a short list of asks and which customers? helps size impact.

Maya: short list: BigRetail (needs 6mo pin), FinCo (pin exception during audit window), EduCloud (requests rolling canary to avoid embed drift). also 2 smaller customers asking for automatic sticky pins for legacy models.

Alina: from CS: BigRetail is on a strict audit timeline; losing pins eats into their cutover plan. FinCo will churn if audit can't be satisfied. EduCloud is lower $$ but high visibility.

Owen: infra note — long-lived pins increase cold-spot capacity pressure and make autoscaler heuristics less effective. we saw a 12% tail latency spike last time when 30% of traffic was pinned to older quant variants.

Maya: thanks. proposed options: 
1) short-term: allow scoped pin-exceptions (30/60/180d) with quota per-account + manual approval.
2) medium: add "grace-path" feature in catalog where model pin decays over time and triggers suggested migrations + customer comms.
3) long-term: self-serve managed compatibility shim and contract add-on.

Simon: option 1 is fastest. who owns approvals? PM + CS + Legal? also need benchmark waiver rules — pinned models should pass a safety/quality smoke.

Alina: CS can own approvals for accounts < $100k ARR. anything enterprise needs legal signoff. we can triage via support tag + short form.

Maya: draft of minimal approval form (example):
```
customer: BigRetail
requested_pin_length: 180d
reason: audit continuity
must_pass: smoke-quality (p0 prompts), perf-check (99p latency), security-scan
owner: CS + PM
```

Owen: we also need a runtime SLA on pinned model capacity. suggest: pinned_capacity_reservation: optional reserve with cost offset. otherwise, pinned models are best-effort and can be auto-rolled to a compatible variant if capacity constrained.

Simon: dev concern — we need an automated benchmark gate to avoid regressions. proposal: when approving a pin, run a lightweight eval suite (10-50 prompts) and store results in the model's catalog entry with a pinned-tag and timestamp. rollback gating uses that snapshot.

Maya: agree. prioritize: short-term (option 1) this sprint (low dev). medium-term (option 2) next quarter for productized flow. long-term on roadmap as FY follow-up.

Alina: customer comms: we'll prep a templated comm for each approved pin (dates + migration playbook + contact).

Maya: decision ask — can eng deliver scoped pin-exceptions + approval UI + smoke-eval in 2 sprints? @simon you + eng estimate?

Simon: rough estimate: approval UI (1 sprint), backend flags + form (0.5 sprint), smoke-eval infra (0.5 sprint) — total ~2. depends on priorities. need to deprioritize one minor item from current sprint backlog.

Owen: infra work for capacity reservations could be separate; for short-term we treat pins as labeled without reservation. we'll track cost impact in console and send weekly usage alerts.

Maya: ok — action items: 
- Simon: scope ticket and list one low-priority thing to slide out (due EOD today).
- Alina: draft approval form + comm templates (tomorrow).
- Owen: add a console metric query for pinned-model tail-latency (end of week).
- Maya: compile customer asks and cc sales for contract exceptions.

deploy-bot: Reminder: weekly roadmap sync in #product at 1600 PT tomorrow :calendar:

Simon: ack. will post scope ticket and ETA by EOD.

Alina: will share comm drafts in thread once ready.

Maya: thanks team — leaning to option 1 for now. will call for a quick decision at tomorrow's sync if we have scoping. :thumbsup:
